Hello V,

I'll give this my best shot. I'm still not 100% on IF's reasoning but I'll give it ago.

1. Price engulfs the high to the left and returns to the decision to engulf below, notice the nice RBR below? well this forms the rally of the bigger RBR. 2. Price FTRs off the decision below (demand) and shoots away, we now have our FL upon the engulf of the new high. 3. Price exhausts itself at 3 and hits the supply at the FO to the left.. 4. We then move slowly down to 4 where we have our FTB to the FL, notice of the way down we removed all of the supply? 5. 3 and 4 define the limits of our flag, at 5 we engulf the upper limit as well as the FO to the left. 6. we try to get back in to the flag at 6 but hit demand at the decision to leave the FLAG. We CP away from 6 removing all of the buy orders. we eventually break 5 and form our FL/FTR. 7. Price then rallies up to 7 where we hit some S/R from the past.

8. At 8 we have our FTB to our FL and we remove the last of the supply. This area shouldn't cause to much of an issue in the future. I believe 8 then becomes the limit of our CPPAZ. 9. at 9 we engulf 7. 10, we fail to return at 10. 11. At 11 we engulf the FL low at 10. 12, we rally and try to get back in to the flag above at 12 then we get rejected by supply at the cap on price. 13. We then start making lower lows and lower highs towards the base of the blue flag we have just entered. 12 is now an important FTR. we are aiming for the supply at the edge of the CPPAZ at 8 where we should get a small reaction at least. 14. we retrace back to the supply above at 14 which is a nice cap on price. 15 At 15 we engulf in to the CPPAZ, and want the other side, we retrace back to the last supply at 14, the origin of the move/decision to engulf. we drop through the CPPAZ and through the other side to the base of the pole at 4 where the sells overwhelmed the little demand that was left it that area.

Now, I'm unsure whether the engulf in to the CPPAZ meant we could expect to drop all the way to the bottom of the blue flag because the CP had effectively removed all of the orders from the FL and this was the barrier to the Blue flag below. Maybe IF can confirm this one to us?

16. So at 16 we engulf the lower limit of the blue flag and also the FL holding it up. 17. price retraces to 17 where there is a strong s/r flip right on the edge of the FTR which was created after engulfing in to the CPPAZ. I don't know why IF put the red box around the swing high? Maybe because it was stacked supply? With the FTR and the CAP? 18. so, we hit of the S/r flip and the FTR which was the edge of the previous zone, which makes sense as we just engulfed in to a new zone at 16. and 15 is the edge of the last FL. 19. From 17 we can take a trade knowing that price wants to go down to the FL at 18 because of the engulf in to the FLAG.

So, to answer your question, i think IF means we should follow the key engulfs of these flags especially when they are forming either side of key s/r levels. as we cross one of these levels and FTR we are flipping sentiment on the value, what was once a great place to buy, is now a great place to sell.

OK so, this is where things aren't straight forward, so how do we define a FLAG? How do we know the limits? after leaving a flag limit, lets say it's a demand FL, how do we know where the high is? is it the point reached before we come back to the demand of the FL, I say this because often we will only hit the s/r of the FL, engulf the high and then come back down to the body/demand of the FL. so would the high of the FLAG in that scenario be define by the high reached upon leaving the FL or the HIGH reached before returning to the body/demand of the FL? I think this is very important for us to nail down, If there is a flag then there is a way of defining it.

IF, can you clear that up for us? To simplify, is the limit the high reached after leaving the FL, i.e. the high of the rally in the RBR? or is it the high reached before the FTB to the demand of the FL? I.E. not the s/r of the FL? I'll draw an example.

Hi all, I've been holding back from posting as i gather my thought's on the exact way I want to trade.

Something I have been having trouble with is clearing defining a trading plan. I'm very aware of my personality type and i need a plan to suit it or I will be doomed to fail. I have been trading a very small account to really pick up on my flaws. I've had mixed results, some very good trades, some trades where my SL has been too close, or another way of putting it is that I've been too greedy. I have jumped in the market when i shouldn't have and I've chased positions.

I've traded at my best when I've made a logical decision and set targets based upon where i think price will turn and not where i want price to go to meet a monetary goal.

My aim is consistency and this is now my main focus, ridding myself of anything that will make me inconsistent. Primarily, actions without reasons.

So far it is quite straight forward creating the plan, the hard part is WHAT I'm going to trade and defining the specific conditions I require. For me, I need this proven concept, something that i can rinse and repeat, day in, day out.

I'm finding it hard to define the concept that suits me, I like the idea of decisions being made rather than price just simply failing to return, the decision to engulf (which is made before an engulf) is logically more important than price failing to return after an engulf. I say this because the decision must be the origin of the imbalance therefore where the orders are, a failure to return is just a reaction, not a decision. When something is a decision and a failure to return that's a whole different thing and I would say is very important.

Where I was going wrong in my definition of FL's was not accepting we can made new FLs as we engulf each FL in a single move. I was placing more importance on the FL that made the most important decision. I now accept this and am happy to stick with it.

Something else that I have been working on is that everything moves in threes and that the institutions are lazy. the strength of their moves are repeated, over and over again and this creates symmetry. we can see this through making basic S/R lines.Id we look at the structure of RBR's and DBD's in every time frame we can see that the moves are measured, they don not look the same but from decision to decision the carry a very similar strength. This is going to require a bit more nailing down but you'll see how it ties in with s and d levels to the left, quite convenient.

That's my 2 cents for the day.

Good trading everyone.

Robbie

Hi Robbie,

You have made quite many insights in your post. First step to fixing anything is finding out what does not work haha

It is always easy to give advice than to follow one

Break it down to small parts and focus on 1 small part.

RTM gives one the edge of reading the market in other terms very high win rate. This is just to make a point and we should not start thinking of expectancies at RTM... (at least my take on it). So even if you would make 1R per trade you could achieve consistent results. Thus... would suggest to forget optimal targets and most optimal SL. Make it simple and easy. Focus on Entries, place SL in rational places and be safer than needed. as far as targets... target first trouble area (so you don't need to think about it) it can be SR flip, DP, FTR, etc.

After you nail entries... focus on another small part... ant then another It is important to break it into parts otherwise there are many variables and too many combinations for the poor brain to manage.

my 2 cents.

Hi Robbie,

Popping by to say hello. Bit of a message to you and others around here as I can observe that RTM does not have the same solid support hierarchy that once upon a time it thrived in. It has taken me the better part of today to read your journal from beginning to end. Great job from the get go, you had me sucked in with your maturing narrative and application of the technical skills you have learned. You ask all the right questions which I can see is driven by your desire to have all the definitive answers. Your lengthy pursuit of discovering a fixed and collectively accepted definition of a FL resonated well with me, and I came to realise it was something I never fully reconciled for myself as I was absorbing the teachings here.

There comes a point in time where ones thirst for finite answers exceeds the information accessable and the support provided, but this is where one must rise above their frustrations and move on with cautious optimism on the back of the valuable knowledge they have gained and their own unique mindset, and I am not just talking about trading here. I can appreciate your comments that the support network didn't even meet your minimum expectations, and can empathise how frustrating that must have felt. It's good to see you are still around because I feel that there is a lot traders can learn from your style of learning, observing, journaling and path of discovery, that seem to be absent in others' threads.

I hope that you have since found ways to accept and manage the ambiguity that exists in trading. I found out that ambiguity is addressed with discipline and adherence to an acceptable risk management plan. Define your tolerances and don't accept anything less, this allows you to accept your losses or 'incorrect judgement'. It's really not talked about at much lenth on RTM, but positive expectancy cannot be realised without kneeling down to the almighty topic of risk management. I think you are already at a point in your trading where you accept you don't have all the answers but can succeed regardless. It's all about learning by doing now, you have circled the theory from every which way and the next level of understanding comes with immersing yourself in the process and not second guessing your decisions in real time.

Unfortunately I had not been around at the right time as part of the support network here, and it was a little hard to read your frustrations go unaddressed as I digested your thread. Don't give up on your pursuit.

p.s. Would love to see more of your analysis in the context of the HTF price structures!

SP

Absolutely brilliant post mate!

I had a read through my journal not to long ago and i could see my ups and downs and how I would go back and forward on what I was thinking. You know, when I first started looking at these methods I would see things and disregard them and no one had mentioned it, I should have trusted myself.

I had many questions, most still unanswered, but maybe because to answer them would have been to give too much away? I don't know, but I've eventually came to my own conclusions that make sense and fit with the methods. The FL was a big bone of contention for me and still is to be honest, maybe the article was valid once upon a time but i believe it is truly out of date now, only because there is a little more to it that we need to be aware of, but again, maybe that's the point.

My pursuit for all of the answers was brutal and was actually quite hard mentally, I realised that this train of thought would actually be my downfall when I come to trade, i needed to realign my expectations and what I wanted from the market, and more importantly how I could achieve it.

I would have loved some constructive direction, especially at the start of the year when I was near enough the only person posting but it never came, with what I know now I believe I could have been helped without someone giving away the answers. I eventually just looked to the charts to figure out each turn in price, it wasn't good enough for me for something like the QM or CP to just been something to look for and work, I had to know why. I believe people starting to learn now should keep this in the back of their minds at all times.

Something else that I help me back was this very simple statement 'only trade the edges', This is the key but it's absolutely useless information unless you know how to define an edge. What I've come to realise is that unless you have a definitive place to put your SL and TP then you probably shouldn't take the trade. There are exceptions but i believe they come with experience. PAZ's are supposed to be the last piece of the puzzle, for me they are the most important piece and they have clearly been my pursuit for a long time now. I now draw my over arching PAZ's and then use them to track important orders.

Risk management, nothing more important I'd say. You could master one set up and barely understand price movements at all but if you know when your set up works and know where you SL and TP should go you are on your way to being successful as long as you have good money management.

The reason i'm still here is because I want to help people, I'm no expert, yet, but my knowledge and experience is increasing all of the time.

I quit my job a few months ago to spend more time with my terminally ill Dad, trading will have to be my income soon. I will carry on posting and helping people for as long as I can.

Discipline, patience and a plan, there is so much more to trading than the charts. We will defeat ourselves of we don't accept our limitations, at least to a degree.

I really appreciate you taking the time to post. I'll put up some HTF analysis later, on USDCHF, I believe we have a big short OP very very close.

Cheers,

Robbie

Nice top down analysis Robbie. It's a very complex top down, due to the large amount of contradictions that become evident in market analysis, and I will do my best to articulate what I am thinking when I absorb your commentary. I have made a few observations about your charts below.

Monthly I largely agree with your views, but am also not attached to the idea, as anything can happen at anytime. That overhead target could take some months (hehe) to get there.

Weekly I typed up a rant about fakeouts but I decided to delete it. I urge you and others to use that term very sparingly and focus on what is real and happening in front of you each and every tick. Price follows the path of least resistance. You have outlined the possible resistance areas perfectly well. Your M5 chart has great confluence with your weekly analysis and your H4 analysis, so great job there. As I type I can see that there is definitely some selling pressure here, but how far it will go, is a mystery. How long you hold your short trade will come down to your pain tolerance and how long you're able to wait, but as the market can do anything at anytime, and make new decisions that were not part of an original analysis, it is important to take profit of the table at logical areas on the chart. I am not particularly convinced that price will head to the lower weekly target before the overhead target and visa versa, and I don't think the market has decided on that yet either, hence why we have had weeks and months of ranging. Let's put it this way, the long term charts are useful to put our shorter term trades into some overall context, they are much much harder to use as long term target practice if you're not the patient type. New decisions have to be made.

H4 Yes, sure, it was an engulf at one point in time, but the whole move that caused the engulf, has been engulfed itself. Pay credence to the new information on the chart, which contradicts your original views. There are many engulfs on a chart that are no longer 'useful' engulfs, as a chart evolves. You will have to discover this for yourself over many laborious months of charting

M5 I like the idea of a touch trade on the upper blue box for entry and the stop above the lower red line. Maximise that risk reward A strategy, if you get stopped out, is to wait for bearish PA on the M5 chart within the entire M30 zone to signal you back in. (For what it's worth your analysis sent some pips my way, I took the trade.)

In summary Because I've crapped on a bit, some things to be mindful of: 1. The word 'fake' often comes with negative connotations and thus 'fakeout' can be harmful, be very careful of the language and terms you use to describe your trading as depending on how you have a term defined in your mind, it will affect how you take action and execute your trading plan. 2. An analysis of a chart in one moment of time will not always be relevant by the time you make the trade. A good analysis requires constant information gathering using multiple time frames and from pre-trade to post-trade.
